claims.text: Integrating machine-learning predictive modeling with thermodynamic analysis enables rapid identification of promising refractory HEA compositions.
The identified compositions will simultaneously have enhanced strength, enhanced ductility, and reduced weight compared with conventionally screened alloys.
Traditional BCC refractory alloys exhibit a strength–ductility trade-off.
Traditional refractory HEAs have higher densities than the proposed optimized alloys.
A data-driven approach combining predictive modeling and thermodynamic analysis can rapidly screen the large multicomponent HEA composition space.
The prediction model is trained on a large, representative dataset for refractory alloy systems.
The optimized alloys will retain a predominantly BCC solid-solution structure.
The optimized alloys will contain coherent precipitate distributions.
Coherent precipitate distributions will reduce stress concentrations.
The optimized microstructure will improve dislocation mobility.
The model can identify compositional regimes that balance lattice distortion with workable dislocation dynamics.
Lattice distortion provides strengthening in the proposed refractory HEAs.
Workable dislocation dynamics provide ductility in the proposed refractory HEAs.
Selecting lower-density elements will reduce alloy density.
Balancing lattice distortion and dislocation dynamics will overcome the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
Predicted compositions will show statistically significant simultaneous improvements in strength, ductility, and weight relative to baseline designs.
Traditional CALPHAD-based or manual alloy-design strategies require extensive computational and experimental resources.
Traditional alloy-design strategies often fail to optimize strength, ductility, and weight simultaneously.
The proposed improvement is expected to apply to refractory HEAs with similar principal elements, such as Nb, Mo, Ta, and W.
Unforeseen minor-phase formation or processing problems may reduce the predicted improvements.
